case_name: Vijay Kumar and Ors v. State of NCT of Delhi and Anr — CRL.M.C. 2188/2022 and Crl.M.A. No.9264/2022

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Vijay Kumar and Ors (husband, wife, etc.)
parties.respondent_defendant: State of NCT of Delhi and Anr (wife, husband, etc.)

facts_of_case: Petitioners seek quashing of FIR No. 444/2016 registered under Sections 406/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. Settlement reached between petitioners and respondent no.2, marriage dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 7.4.2022 in HMA No. 22/478.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
legal_principles.held: On the other, those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
cited_cases: Narender Singh &Ors. V. State of Punjab; (2014) 6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: It is not safe to leave the crime-doer only because he and the victim have settled the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation, yet certain crimes have been made compoundable in law, with or without the permission of the court.
legal_principles.held: No doubt, crimes are acts which have harmful effect on the public and consist in wrongdoing that seriously endangers and threatens the well-being of the society and it is not safe to leave the crime-doer only because he and the victim have settled the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation, yet certain crimes have been made compoundable in law, with or without the permission of the court.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Another, (2012) 10 SCC 303

keywords: Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act
